title: Granular Access Control for Medical Records
business: Healthcare providers managing sensitive patient data across multi-disciplinary teams.
problem: Unauthorized staff members are accessing patient records outside their assigned department, leading to potential privacy violations and compliance failures.
solution: Implement Complete Mediation by enforcing authorization checks on every request to ensure that only users with explicit, role-based permissions can access specific patient records.
steps: Define granular roles such as Physician, Nurse, and Billing Clerk.
Map each role to specific resource actions like ReadRecord or UpdateBilling.
Implement a central authorization service that validates the user's token and requested action against the resource policy.
Enforce the check at the API gateway level to ensure every incoming request is mediated before reaching the database.
Audit all authorization decisions to ensure compliance with privacy regulations.
outcome: A secure environment where access is strictly limited to the minimum necessary information, reducing the risk of unauthorized data exposure.
limitation: The primary trade-off is latency, as performing a check on every request adds overhead; this can be monitored by tracking the response time of the authorization service.

questions.question: In Granular Access Control for Medical Records, why is Complete Mediation used?
options: To ensure authority is not circumvented by checking rights upon every request.
To improve system performance by caching user roles in the database.
To allow users to define their own access levels for better usability.
To hide the implementation details of the database from the user.
questions.explanation: Complete Mediation ensures that access requests are checked every time to prevent unauthorized access.
questions.evidence: Implement Complete Mediation by enforcing authorization checks on every request to ensure that only users with explicit, role-based permissions can access specific patient records.
